facts: In 1954, L formed a company for aerial top-dressing and held almost all of its shares. He was appointed governing director and employed as the chief pilot under an article of association. In March 1956, L was killed in a flying accident while piloting the company's aircraft. His widow claimed compensation under the Workers' Compensation Act, 1922, as a dependant of a worker.
issue: Whether L could be a 'worker' working under a contract of service with the company, given that he was also the sole governing director and controlling shareholder.
held: The court decided that L was a worker entitled to compensation because the company was a distinct legal entity. His special position as governing director did not prevent him from making a valid contract of employment with the company.
principle: A company is a separate legal entity distinct from its shareholders and directors, which allows a controlling shareholder and director to also enter into a valid contract of service with the company.
points: A company is a distinct legal person separate from its members.
A controlling shareholder and director can also be an employee of the company.
Dual roles, such as being both a governing director and a servant, are legally possible.
The right of control can exist even if the same individual exercises management and gives orders on behalf of the company.
